science.title: Predicting fish spoilage through adsorption and detection of volatile sulfur compounds on B2N monolayers: a computational study
science.description: In the present work, a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation was conducted to elucidate the adsorption behavior of two key sulfur-containing volatile compounds generated during fish deterioration, namely dimethyl sulfide (DMS, CH₃–S–CH₃) and dimethyl disulfide (DMDS, CH₃–S–S–CH₃). The calculated adsorption energies are significantly negative, revealing strong yet reversible adsorption characteristics suitable for both sensing and capture applications. The obtained Eads (%ΔEg) values for DMS/B₂N and DMDS/B₂N are − 0.47 eV (40%) and − 0.45 eV (39%), respectively. Adsorption induces substantial modulation of the B₂N electronic band gap, generating distinct electronic responses for each analyte. As a result, the monolayer exhibits distinct electronic and φ-type sensing responses, arising from substantial band-gap modulation and charge transfer between the adsorbed species and the B₂N substrate, thereby providing a pronounced and readily detectable electrical response. The pristine B₂N surface exhibits high sensitivity toward both DMS and DMDS, while the short recovery times and ultrafast desorption confirm excellent reversibility. Therefore, the B₂N monolayer serves as a multifunctional nanomaterial, acting as both a high-performance sensor and an efficient adsorbent for sulfur-based spoilage compounds, and presents a promising strategy for real-time seafood freshness monitoring.

science.title: Quantum similarity estimation with hybrid discrete-continuous encoding: algorithm and application to atomtronics precision measurements
science.description: We introduce a quantum similarity estimation algorithm which employs an entangled discrete-continuous representation and a modified SWAP-test protocol using conditional displacement and controlled-SWAP operations. The corresponding exact form of the similarity metric is analytically derived and its feasible circuit implementation is provided. We apply this result to interferometric images, which are numerically generated from an experimentally viable atomtronics setup. A ring-shaped potential, confining a localized Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), is considered where the BEC manifests fractional revivals during its confined time-evolution. We perform a precise identification of nonlinearity, originated from interatomic interactions, which can be tuned by Feshbach resonance and thus, the presented method paves the possibility for a magnetic field sensor. Moreover, we perform quantum simulation with Shot-noise of the proposed quantum circuit with public benchmark datasets and analyse the resource and computational complexities of the proposed algorithm.
